title: Statewide three-layer data audit — WRITTEN / SCORED / SERVED
status: HONEST PARTIAL CLOSE, REOPENED AND WIDENED 2026-08-19 on operator ruling. WRITTEN and SCORED are measured statewide and complete. The SERVED layer's first run was STOPPED at 33 counties because it measured NINE fields against FOURTEEN rails; it has been widened to all fourteen and restarted statewide as a detached job. Nothing is reported as a zero that was not measured.
missionPremise: OPS-16 amendments A-018 and A-019. P-43 delivered two counties of 253 and the operator's L26 screenshots corrected the planner's frame: the audit is THREE layers, not two. WRITTEN atoms in the store, SCORED ledger cells, SERVED what a human is shown, all disagreeing independently. The order of the disagreement is the cost of the fix — written-unscored is a scorer run, written-unserved is a merge fix, only genuinely unwritten is a re-ingest — so a gap reported without its class invites somebody to scope a re-ingest for a merge bug. The operator's live question was footprints: landed in 174 counties closing 2026-08-17 12:43Z, while the ledger reports not-yet on all 254 cells because it was computed 67 hours earlier.
completionPredicate: A stranger can (1) run `node --import tsx packages/retrieval/scripts/three-layer-audit.mjs --out <dir> --served-dir <sweepdir>` against the two production stores and get a document conforming to StatewideServingSweep with one additive threeLayer field, carrying all three layers per rail per county with their own counts and their own denominators; (2) verify the classifier's zeros are not dead gates by running `npx vitest run src/statewide-audit/__tests__/classify.test.ts`, which proves every GapClass can fire and that mutating one input moves the verdict; and (3) read a dated report that answers the footprint question with its denominator and classifies every gap into the three remediation classes. All three hold today. The one part NOT complete is the statewide SERVED sweep, which is running detached and is reported as not-measured wherever it has not landed.
scopeBasis: The dispatch scoped the statewide audit as a background job and named footprints as the first validation case. The WRITTEN and SCORED layers are cheap enough to finish inside one session (17 serialized index scans plus one full-table roster scan, about 80 minutes of database time in total) and they are where the finding turned out to be, so they were run to completion statewide. The SERVED layer is the only expensive one and it was launched detached rather than sampled, because sampling is what certified a broken Bastrop once. No county was cherry-picked: the sweep runs all 254 in ascending FIPS order.

theFootprintAnswer.question: footprints landed in 174 counties and the ledger says not-yet on 254 — which layer is lying
theFootprintAnswer.verdict: NEITHER. All three layers are telling the truth about different things, and the dispatch's staleness framing is half right in a way that changes the remediation.

WRITTEN.label: VERIFIED by this lane
WRITTEN.countingRule: atom ROWS keyed <fips>:<propId>:footprint:<slot>; the parcel figure is the footprint:primary slot, one per parcel that has any footprint
WRITTEN.theThingNobodyAsked: NOT ONE METRO IS AMONG THE 174. Bastrop 48021, Travis 48453, Harris 48201, Dallas 48113, Williamson 48491 and Bexar 48029 all hold ZERO. Verified twice, by a GROUP BY on the entity_id prefix and independently by a prefix LIKE probe. The 174 are the cheap rural counties, led by Wise 48497 (65,056), Van Zandt 48467 (56,468) and Victoria 48469 (53,584), which matches the rail's own stated limitation that O(fp x parcels) compute limits metro-scale apply.

SCORED.label: VERIFIED by this lane
SCORED.theCorrection: STALENESS IS NOT THE MECHANISM. There is NO footprint row in county_facet_coverage at all — not a stale row, no row. The manifest grid resolves rail_state IS NULL to not-yet by display precedence, so RECOMPUTING THE LEDGER WOULD LEAVE ALL 254 CELLS EXACTLY WHERE THEY ARE. The remediation is a footprint scorer, which does not exist. Lane SS-W7 is building a recompute route; it is necessary and it is not sufficient, and SS-W7 should be told so.

SERVED.label: VERIFIED by this lane against the deployed surface
SERVED.result: HTTP 200, X-Pe-Read-Path: atom-chain-warm, 2045 bytes, 69 key paths
SERVED.finding: NONE of the 69 key paths is a footprint. The parcel fact sheet has no slot for the rail at all, so no merge could surface it. Adding a served field is a larger job than a merge fix and must not be priced as one.
SERVED.secondProbeOnAParcelThatHASAFootprint: The Bastrop probe proves the sheet has no footprint slot, but Bastrop has no footprint atoms, so on its own it could be read as a coverage gap rather than a missing field. Two Wise County 48497 parcels that DO carry building-footprint atoms in the store were probed on the deployed surface: 48497:200000002 and 48497:200000104, both HTTP 200, X-Pe-Read-Path: atom-chain, 617 bytes, 30 key paths each, ZERO matches for footprint, easement, owner, special district, well, pipeline, corridor, tier2, frontage or attachingRoads. WRITTEN yes, SCORED no, SERVED no, on one parcel, all three layers at once. Wise is the largest footprint county in the state with 65,056 atoms.

classification.note: One rail, three different remediations, three different prices. That is the whole reason the audit is three layers.

gapClassTotals.countingRule: one cell per county per rail, 254 x 14; classified by packages/retrieval/src/statewide-audit/classify.ts
gapClassTotals.whyNoGapIsZero: A cell reaches no-gap only when the SERVED layer has been measured for it, and the statewide sweep was still running at close. The 393 not-measured cells are the written-and-scored ones waiting on it; they resolve to no-gap or written-unserved and nowhere else. Stated rather than hidden, because a zero from an unrun measurement is exactly the defect shape this programme hunts.
gapClassTotals.outOfReachCaveat: The rule is coarse by necessity: the capability probe reports a COUNT, not a SET, so no instrument here can say WHICH counties are reachable. 239 of the 241 are owner, whose ceiling of 15 equals the number of counties whose CAD roll is loaded. The other 2 are rail-corridor at 252 written against a ceiling of 253, where at least one of the two is genuinely reachable and is being called out-of-reach by the coarseness of the rule.

headlineFinding.finding: 1,170 of 3,556 cells hold atoms and no satisfied ledger cell, carrying 59,744,770 atom rows. None of them is an ingestion problem.
headlineFinding.theWorsePart: SIX of fourteen rails have ZERO rows in county_facet_coverage: roads, footprint, easement, rrc-wells, rrc-pipelines, rail-corridor. That is 1,524 of 3,556 cells, 42.9% of the manifest grid, permanently not-yet regardless of the store. 951 of those county-cells ARE written, holding 35,159,990 atom rows behind a ledger that no recompute can move.
headlineFinding.mechanism: hauska-engine ships TWELVE county writers. legacy-design-tools ships THREE scorer CLIs (countyCoverageScoreCli.ts, countyFloodScoreCli.ts, countyGeometryScoreCli.ts). Twelve producers, three consumers. And most of the ledger was not written by those three: verified_by_instrument shows cad/landuse/owner (254 rows each) came from score_cad_rails_fast.mjs, geometry from B2_cp2_geometry_scorer_apply.mjs and l16-score-geometry-48201.mjs, mud from l16-score-mud.mjs. Only flood (177 rows) and one geometry cell name a checked-in CLI. The SCORED layer is largely the residue of one-off lane scripts, which is the mechanical reason no recompute route exists.

findings.finding: NINE of fourteen rails have no key path on the served payload at all. Only FIVE can reach a human through this endpoint.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED by the negative control in rail-served.test.ts, run against the REAL production body captured from https://property-explorer-xi.vercel.app/api/spine/property-atoms/48021:36521/facets (HTTP 200, X-Pe-Read-Path atom-chain-warm, 2045 bytes, 69 key paths). Rails with a slot: cad, envelope, geometry, landuse, zoning. Rails with NO slot: easement, flood, footprint, mud, owner, rail-corridor, roads, rrc-pipelines, rrc-wells.
findings.thisCorrectsMyOwnEarlierReport: I reported SEVEN slotless rails, derived from the frozen FieldKey union. The measured answer is NINE. flood and roads are NAMED in FieldKey, so a reader of the record would assume both are served, and neither has a key path on the real wire: tier2 is absent from the body entirely and attachingRoads is never copied by the PE adapter. The test assertion was written expecting seven and FAILED, which is the entire reason it exists. Both the report and this close are corrected to nine.
findings.consequence: geometry's only slot is /facets/envelope/geojson — the buildable-envelope polygon. The sheet carries no parcel ring at all, which is contract invariant I5 inverted and is why a missing address presents as a broken Find.

findings.finding: rrc-pipelines and rail-corridor are ALREADY on the retrieval wire and the adapter drops them. That is the cheapest remediation class, and the nine-field sweep could not see it.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED on a 300-parcel instrument smoke run over Bastrop 48021 with the widened runner: rrc-pipeline-fact and rail-corridor-fact resolve on-wire-not-served for 295 of 300 parcels, no-slot-in-payload for the other 5. The atoms ride the assembled chain the PE BFF consumes; the adapter has no field for them. 12,519,688 rrc-pipeline-fact atoms across 250 counties and 13,059,613 rail-corridor-fact atoms across 252 counties are in that position statewide, pending the full run.
findings.whyItMatters: Before the widening these two rails would have been scoped as new product fields. They are an adapter reading a field it already receives. That is exactly the mis-pricing the three-layer record exists to prevent, and the narrow sweep would have caused it.
findings.caveat: The 300-parcel figure is an INSTRUMENT smoke run, not a coverage claim. The statewide number comes from the restarted sweep.

findings.finding: The rrc-wells capability ceiling contradicts the store AND its own basis string, and it points the OPPOSITE way from the standing finding.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED: well-fact is written in 174 counties — 2,041,196 atoms naming a real API number plus 2,297,099 positive-absence atoms with the none suffix, 4,338,295 rows total. Harris 48201, the ONE county the ceiling names, holds ZERO (confirmed twice, by GROUP BY and by an independent prefix probe). The live probe on GET /api/county-ledger reports rrc-wells maxCountiesReachable 1, reachPct 0.0039. Its own sourceBasis reads 'RRC public GIS Harris County mirror carries STATEWIDE well coverage' — the hostname is Harris, the data is statewide, and a ceiling of 1 read the host rather than the sentence. The 174 counties are led by Callahan 48103 (58,557 wells), Wilbarger 48475 (55,192), Sterling 48401 (52,893), Yoakum 48501 (51,684) and Menard 48317 (46,592), which is where Texas wells are.
findings.notResolvedHere: Either the hardcoded ceiling is wrong, or 2,041,196 well atoms and 2,297,099 absence determinations are wrong across 173 counties. Very different remediations; the call is the planner's. What is certain is that scoring rrc-wells today against a ceiling of 1 would classify 173 genuinely-written counties as out-of-reach.
findings.standingMemoryAffected: The standing note that the RRC wells source is HARRIS-ONLY with 12,796 features, and that applying outside 48201 writes mass false-negative absences, is contradicted by the store as it stands today and should be re-adjudicated rather than carried forward unchanged.

findings.finding: A live scorer writes a facet name the ledger read path cannot join.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED: countyCoverageScoreCli.ts writes facet 'land-use' (hyphenated). The rail key is 'landuse'. readManifestGrid joins c.facet = r.rail_key. 'land-use' is the ONLY facet in county_facet_coverage matching no rail — 19 rows, orphaned, read by nothing.

findings.finding: The store says 19 zoning cells are satisfied; the console shows 1.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED: county_facet_coverage holds 19 rows with rail_state satisfied-present for zoning, of which only 1 is at or above its threshold (mean honest_coverage_pct 8.59). applyDepthRailDisplayGate demotes the other 18 to not-yet at read time. Both numbers are defensible and they are 19 apart; anyone quoting either must name which.

findings.finding: The checked-in rail declaration disagrees with the live county_rail table in BOTH directions, and with the store.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED: live county_rail says all 14 rails are atom_family_state present with has_writer true. countyRailDimension.ts says roads, footprint and easement have no writer and that rrc-wells, rrc-pipelines and rail-corridor have no atom family. Six of fourteen rows differ. The declaration is also wrong about the store: 12,519,688 rrc-pipeline-fact and 13,059,613 rail-corridor-fact atoms exist, so those families are not missing.

findings.finding: rrc-pipelines is bound to NO atom family while the store holds 12.5 million of its atoms.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED: RAIL_ENGINE_BINDINGS for rrc-pipelines carries an empty atomEntityTypes array; rrc-pipeline-fact holds 12,519,688 atoms across 250 counties. Any derivation reading that binding concludes the rail cannot exist. This audit names the family explicitly in RAIL_ATOM_FAMILIES and files the disagreement rather than silently picking a side.

findings.finding: flood has no ledger row at all in 77 counties, and the manifest renders that identically to a scored-and-short cell.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED: 177 rows for a 254-cell rail, 114 satisfied. So flood's 140 not-yet cells are two different things — 63 scored and below bar, 77 never scored — and nothing on the surface distinguishes them. WRITTEN meanwhile is 253 counties and 13,197,039 atoms, so 139 written cells are unsatisfied, holding 11,532,633 rows.

findings.finding: utility-easement is the only genuinely empty family, and it is the one rail whose 254 not-yet cells are honest.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED: zero rows, scan returned in 0 seconds. hauska-engine ships write-utility-easement-county.mjs and it has never been run.

findings.finding: The address ladder has at least SIX rungs, not four, and the sixth is not a sentinel — it is a road reference stored in the city column.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED by this lane, txgio_parcel, 253 counties, DISTINCT prop_id per county summed, denominator 13,071,975. non-null 12,999,845 (99.45%), non-blank 12,999,845 (99.45%), carries-a-street 11,751,433 (89.90%) — all three reproduce SS-W5 TO THE PARCEL. carries-a-city measures 8,179,225 (62.57%) against SS-W5's 8,178,863, 362 parcels apart across 48 counties, led by Gillespie 48171 (+263) and Cameron 48061 (+20). RUNG FIVE: 11 parcels across 8 counties carry a situs_city that is non-blank with no alphanumeric at all (a comma, a backslash, an asterisk, an apostrophe, an at-sign, and ????), the same defect as the address sentinel one column over. RUNG SIX: in Gillespie, 11,827 parcels carry a non-blank situs_city whose most common values are OFF E US HWY 290 (1,305), OFF S RANCH ROAD 783 (693) and OFF W US HWY 290 (505) — road references that pass non-null, non-blank AND alphanumeric. No rule proposed so far catches them.
findings.unreconciled: SS-W5's exact city predicate is not recorded in the merged source, so the 362 cannot be attributed. Both numbers are published with their rules; neither is quietly preferred.

findings.finding: SUPERSEDED BY F0 — this said SEVEN of fourteen rails have no served slot. The measured answer is NINE. Kept, corrected in place, because the wrong number was published and deleting it would hide that a control caught it.
findings.evidence: The original evidence stands as far as it went: the live body for 48021:36521 carries 69 key paths and none for footprint, easement, owner, special district, well, pipeline or rail corridor, and owner is stripped by design. What it got WRONG was flood and roads. Both are NAMED in the frozen FieldKey union, so both were assumed served; neither has a key path on the wire. See F0 for the measured nine, and F0b for the two of the nine that are an adapter fix rather than a new field.
findings.consequence: That is a product decision about what a parcel sheet is for, not a pipeline bug, and it should be made deliberately rather than inherited from whichever fields the first adapter happened to carry.

findings.finding: THIS LANE'S OWN FIRST SCAN SCRIPT HAD TWO CONTROLS THAT COULD NOT FAIL.
findings.evidence: (1) It issued SET statement_timeout as its own psql -c, which is a separate transaction, so the timeout never applied to the query it was meant to bound and every scan ran unbounded. The runner now sets it as a connection STARTUP parameter. (2) Its first version had an invalid GROUP BY and failed 25 of 25 queries while still printing WRITTEN SCAN DONE; the script now fails loudly on any non-zero rc. Both are the same defect class this programme hunts — a control that cannot fail is not a control — and they are recorded because catching them in my own instrument is the only reason to trust its output.

findings.finding: main's pnpm-lock.yaml has been out of sync with packages/retrieval/package.json since SS-W5 merged.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED: f12c3ea added postgres ^3.4.5 to packages/retrieval/package.json and the lockfile was never regenerated. CI survives it only because both workflows install with --frozen-lockfile=false. Fixed on this branch in 06e442d.

controlsProvenAbleToFail: County key derivation: verifyCountyKey compares split_part(entity_id, colon, 1) against body countyFips for every parcel-node atom and THROWS on any disagreement rather than footnoting it. Result: 0 disagreeing atoms of 13,717,341. The gate ran for 8.7 minutes and the whole run is downstream of it.
Gap classifier liveness: 17 tests prove every GapClass can fire on constructed input. Run green: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 17 passed (17).

Gap classifier divergence: four cases mutate ONE input each and assert the verdict moves, including that scorer-absent and ledger-stale must never read the same, because one is a build and the other is a run.
Ledger probe: asserts content-type as well as status, so an SPA HTML fallthrough is reported as a failure and never as an empty ledger.

Independent re-derivation: every headline WRITTEN figure was produced twice, once by a GROUP BY on the entity_id prefix and once by a prefix LIKE probe. Callahan well-fact 60,396 = 1,839 absence + 58,557 wells under both shapes; utility-easement 0; footprint 0 in Bastrop, Travis and Harris under both.

Instrument re-run against another lane: the SERVED sweep's Bastrop 48021 record reproduces SS-W5's tallies EXACTLY, field for field, 24 hours later — geometry 3,931, situsAddress 46,144, apn 62,399, landUse 61,531, zoning 9,557, setbacks 3,931, envelope 3,931, flood 0, frontage 0, of 62,399; roster union 62,399; unresolvable 0. SS-W5's Bastrop figures are therefore VERIFIED by this lane, not relayed.

Fourteen-rail SERVED detector liveness: 29 tests prove EVERY rail's detector fires on a payload that carries its slot, that `mud` does NOT false-positive on facets.zoning.district or facets.envelope.district, that an UNAVAILABLE wire probe never manufactures on-wire-not-served, and that a payload gaining a facet key or gaining tier2 changes its shape signature so a newly-served rail can never be memoised away. Full retrieval suite: 13 files, 116 tests passed; typecheck exit 0.

The negative control CORRECTED THE REPORT IT WAS CHECKING. It was written asserting seven slotless rails, taken from my own published finding, and it failed: the real body has nine. A control that only ever confirms the author is not a control.

constraintsHonored: READ ONLY on both production databases: no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or DDL issued.
No atoms bulk-writer slot, no database lease, no --apply.
Heavy scans strictly serialized, one at a time, each announced in the progress artifact before it started and confirmed after.
Every verification command exit-bounded: no watch, no tail, no unbounded scan. statement_timeout on the runner rides connection startup parameters so it actually applies.
Two watches registered in _catalog/watch_registry.json BEFORE their runners started.
Isolated worktree. Branch pushed immediately after the first commit. PR #348 opened against main, CI conclusion string success, NOT merged, NOT deployed, nothing pushed to main.
Every coverage figure travels with its denominator; classes are measured, never subtracted.
No sub-agents spawned; this lane executed as the deepest worker, in sequence, in its own context.
whatRemainsOpen: The widened statewide SERVED sweep is in flight. Until it lands, every unswept county is not-measured and no-gap is legitimately zero. Regenerate with --written-from against P:/tmp/ss_w9_20260819/served14.
The rrc-wells ceiling-versus-store contradiction is FILED, not resolved. The planner has marked the standing Harris-only memory CONTESTED rather than deleted, which is the right disposition.
SS-W5's exact city predicate is unrecovered, so the 362-parcel ladder divergence is named rather than reconciled.
`out-of-reach` is decided from a count and not a set. A set-valued capability probe would sharpen 241 cells.
This audit measures existence, scoring and serving. It does NOT measure whether a written atom is correct.
contradictingTheBriefing: The dispatch says footprint's ledger gap is staleness. It is not: there is no footprint row in county_facet_coverage at all, so a recompute would not move a single one of the 254 cells. Staleness is real and separately measured at 116.3 hours, but it is not the mechanism here, and the distinction changes the remediation from a refresh to a build.

The dispatch says to score every rail against its railCapabilities ceiling. Done — and for rrc-wells the ceiling is the thing that is wrong. Applying it as briefed would have manufactured 173 false out-of-reach classifications, which is the same error the instruction exists to prevent, pointing the other way.

The dispatch frames the three-layer disagreement as this lane's finding to make. The larger finding is upstream of all three: SIX of fourteen rails have no scorer at all, so the SCORED layer cannot converge on the WRITTEN layer for 42.9% of the grid no matter how often anything is recomputed.

The three-layer record I designed was itself asymmetric and I did not catch it before launching a four-hour job on it. The operator did. Recorded here rather than smoothed over, because the lane's own instrument defects are the only reason to trust the rest of its output.

instrumentLimitations.limitation: The `unwritten` class conflates NOT ACQUIRED with POSITIVELY DETERMINED ABSENT, for the rails whose writers emit no absence atom.
instrumentLimitations.detail: Some writers DO record absence positively and this instrument counts it correctly: well-fact carries 2,297,099 atoms with the `none` suffix and special-district-fact carries 4,978,452 with `sd:outside`, both of which are real determinations that nothing is there. Zoning does not: 235 counties have no zoning-fact atom, and most of unincorporated Texas is GENUINELY UNZONED, which is a first-class satisfied-absent state and not a backlog. This audit calls those 235 cells `unwritten`, which overstates the work owed. The statewide `unwritten` total of 1,530 must therefore be read as an UPPER BOUND on acquisition work, not an estimate of it.
instrumentLimitations.howToClose: Either the zoning writer emits a positive-absence atom the way the wells and special-district writers already do, or the audit reads the roster's zoning-regime doctrine rows as a separate input. Neither is in this lane's scope, and guessing which of the 235 are genuinely unzoned would be exactly the fabrication this programme forbids.

instrumentLimitations.limitation: `out-of-reach` is decided from a COUNT, never a SET.
instrumentLimitations.detail: The capability probe reports maxCountiesReachable as a number, so no instrument here can say WHICH counties a rail's source can reach. The rule used is: a rail is at its ceiling when it holds atoms in at least as many counties as the ceiling names. 239 of 241 out-of-reach cells are owner, whose ceiling of 15 equals the loaded CAD-roll county count. The other 2 are rail-corridor at 252 written against a ceiling of 253, where at least one of the two empty counties is genuinely reachable and is being mislabelled by the coarseness of the rule.

instrumentLimitations.limitation: This audit measures EXISTENCE, SCORING and SERVING. It does not measure CORRECTNESS.
instrumentLimitations.detail: A county can be present on all three layers and hold wrong data. The rrc-wells contradiction is the live example: 2,041,196 well atoms exist and this instrument cannot say whether they are right.

instrumentLimitations.limitation: The SERVED field set was established from four parcels across three counties and three read paths, plus the frozen FieldKey union and the vendored adapter source.
instrumentLimitations.detail: 48021:36521 (atom-chain-warm), 48497:200000002 and 48497:200000104 (atom-chain), and three atom-pending responses. All agree that no body carries a footprint, easement, owner, special-district, well, pipeline, rail-corridor, tier2 or frontage slot. That is strong but it is not every read path in every county, and it is stated as what it is.

operatorRulingMidLane.ruling: Do the sweep right the first time. Stop the running served sweep, widen it, restart it. Do not let the current run finish.
operatorRulingMidLane.theDefect: The frozen serving-sweep record carries NINE FieldKey values (geometry, situsAddress, apn, landUse, zoning, setbacks, envelope, flood, frontage) against FOURTEEN rails. The five never asked about were footprint, easement, owner, rrc-wells and rrc-pipelines — and FOUR of those five sit in the six-rail set this lane proved has no scorer at all. So the SERVED layer was blind on exactly the rails already invisible on WRITTEN and SCORED. Footprint is the operator's live question and it had to be hand-probed on two Wise County parcels precisely because the sweep did not cover it. The planner verified this at source in the branch.
operatorRulingMidLane.myAssessment: The ruling is correct and the defect is mine. I built the three-layer record, saw that seven rails had no served slot, hand-probed around the gap, and then launched a four-hour job on the narrow field set anyway. Hand-probing around an instrument's blind spot is the signal to fix the instrument, not to work around it.

That is the nested-orphan trap and it is recorded because a tree kill that reports SUCCESS is not proof the work stopped.

widenedServedLayer.frozenRecordUntouched: serving-sweep/types.ts is still byte-for-byte the planner's frozen record. The new runner emits the nine-field CountyServingSweep UNCHANGED plus an additive `railServed` tally, both computed from the SAME composed body in the SAME pass, so the two cannot drift. An invariant is disputed by reporting, never by editing the contract inside a lane.

fourStatesFourPrices.served: a slot path carries a value
fourStatesFourPrices.slot-empty: a slot exists and resolves empty for this parcel
fourStatesFourPrices.on-wire-not-served: no slot, and the retrieval chain carries the atom — an ADAPTER reading a field it already receives
fourStatesFourPrices.no-slot-in-payload: no key path in the served body could carry this rail — a NEW FIELD on the product surface

widenedServedLayer.absenceIsMeasuredNotSkipped: A rail with no field on the sheet is not omitted. The real payload is inspected, no key path is found that could carry it, and noSlotInPayload is recorded WITH the paths looked at, the token list used, and the count of distinct payload shapes seen. 29 tests in src/statewide-audit/__tests__/rail-served.test.ts prove every rail's detector FIRES on a payload that carries its slot, so the zeros are measurements.
widenedServedLayer.authorityRule: fieldTallyAuthority keeps one rail from carrying two contradictory numbers. For the seven rails that have a nine-field FieldTally, the FieldTally is AUTHORITATIVE for coverage because it applies the real Fact-state logic (the street-segment address rule, the envelope decline logic) that a key-path probe cannot see. The slot tally answers only the narrower slot question. Publishing the slot number as coverage would restate the 99.3%-situs mistake in a new column. For the seven rails with no FieldTally, the slot tally is the only measurement there is — which is the entire reason the widening was necessary.
widenedServedLayer.wireProbeHonesty: Eight rails whose atom family carries a SUFFIXED entity_id cannot ride the id-equality probe, so their on-wire position is reported as UNAVAILABLE rather than false. An absent probe is not an absence. Their store position is already measured per county by the WRITTEN layer. The two families whose entity_id IS the parcel node id (rrc-pipeline-fact, rail-corridor-fact) were added to the chain read at no extra query cost, which is what made the on-wire finding below possible at all.
